💡 Pawnix | Python
🎯 Primary Use Case: Playing chess in the terminal, with seamless integration for local games and online Lichess matches.
✨ Key Features: • Local two-player chess with clocks, SAN/UCI input, undo/redo, PGN import/export • Lichess integration for AI games, online matches, and challenges via Board API • OAuth with PKCE for browser-based Lichess sign-in • Customizable interface with 15 board themes, adjustable piece sizes, and visual aids • Public Lichess profile lookup
📖 Summary: Pawnix is a Python-based, keyboard-first chess client designed for the terminal. It offers both local two-player games and online play through the Lichess API, supporting features like AI practice, matchmaking, and challenges.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

✨ waytator | C
🎯 Primary Use Case: Capturing and editing visual media (screenshots and video recordings) on Wayland display servers.
✨ Key Features: • Screenshot and video recording on Wayland • Image annotation • Video editing (cropping, trimming, rotation, muting, speed changes, etc.) • OCR support • Integration with wlroots-based compositors
📖 Summary: Waytator is a C-based tool for capturing screenshots and recording video on Wayland compositors, also offering basic image and video editing capabilities. It supports features like annotation, cropping, trimming, and audio manipulation, with OCR support for text recognition.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

💡 ytconverter | Python
🎯 Primary Use Case: Downloading and converting YouTube videos from the command line.
✨ Key Features: • Video Downloading • Audio Downloading • Multiple video download • Subtitles download support • Playlist download
📖 Summary: YTConverter is a Python-based command-line interface (CLI) tool designed for downloading and converting YouTube videos. It supports various formats, resolutions, playlists, and subtitles, offering a user-friendly interactive experience directly from the terminal.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

🌟 IPTV | Python
🎯 Primary Use Case: To provide users with a curated list of free, globally accessible TV channels in an M3U format for playback on IPTV-compatible devices and software.
✨ Key Features: • M3U playlist format • Collection of free TV channels • Global channel coverage • Links to publicly available streams
📖 Summary: This repository provides an M3U playlist containing links to free TV channels from around the world. It aims to aggregate publicly available streams for easy access via IPTV players.
🔗 Links: • View Project ================ 🔓 Open Source

🔥 helix | Rust
🎯 Primary Use Case: A highly efficient and modern text editing experience for developers, particularly those who appreciate modal editing paradigms and advanced code intelligence.
✨ Key Features: • Vim-like modal editing • Multiple selections • Built-in language server support • Smart, incremental syntax highlighting and code editing via tree-sitter
📖 Summary: Helix is a post-modern modal text editor written in Rust, inspired by Kakoune and Neovim. It focuses on a unique editing model with multiple selections and integrates advanced features like built-in language server support and smart syntax highlighting via tree-sitter.
🔗 Links: • View Project • Homepage ================ 🔓 Open Source
